recap.text: Odette uses a mask and a crab to appear as a Princess who won a beauty contest. She tells Carl to pick a pathfinder skill, ignore the AI on race, and choose a high charisma option for the Princess. Odette pushed Mordecai too hard in the past and warns Carl about a corporation with a fleet outside the Borant system.

Odette gives the Princess a class that lets her choose another every level. Odette warns Carl that Hekla is practical and cunning and wants Donut to get Mordecai. Odette bought their rights early and would lose her contract if Donut joins Brynhild's Daughters. She warns Carl that a gauntlet can summon a war god whose celebrants the Skull Empire sponsored.

On air, Carl hopes Odette's winnings covered her losses sponsoring Hekla. Odette tells the audience her husband, who sleeps in the skiff, is responsible. After a mute cuts her question about Eva, Odette moves to the next floor's preview. Off air, Odette tells Carl she was the one responsible and that his smoldering anger plays well.

Lexis holds Beatrice in a camp in what used to be Seattle. Lexis killed a sac pirate, captured his null partner, and shot a human. The null lives with a planted weapon while the human expires. Beatrice goes to Borant in a bounty cube, but Odette will not sell her because she has a much better use for her.

Odette tells Carl that Beatrice is alive and that she took her off the planet. She explains that in three of four possible outcomes, others find Beatrice and use her against Carl to end a crawl. Odette asks if Mordecai told Carl what she did to him and requests permission to bring Beatrice on.

Odette refuses to pay Huanxin Jinx fifty per cent of a bonus. She tells Chaco to worship Dodola and put a dart in Uzzi, which kills the goddess and opens the stairwell. Odette tells Carl that worlds are burned for fuel and she intends to shut the business down.

Odette fills in for Chaco, who feels punched in the face. She wears a yellow shirt with her hair in a bun, lacking her mask, breastplate, and crab. Odette onboards into the Ascendency as Nekhebit for a council sponsored by the Ultima Corporation. After Cascadia laughs in her face, Odette takes the meeting.

beats.headline: We have been watching from the beginning
beats.text: The Princess walks on, rolls over halfway to the couch, and has the room before she sits down. She is earth royalty, she tells my audience; among cats it is an elective monarchy, which is to say a beauty contest, and she has won it. Carl does not know his catchphrase, so I show him clip after clip of himself saying it until he does. Will they stay with Meadow Lark? For now. Then she stands on the pillow and promises they will kill with style, and they cheer for thirty seconds.
beats.gist: Odette tells her audience she won an elective monarchy beauty contest among cats.

beats.headline: Tell Mordecai to find me
beats.text: Off air, the mask comes off, then the chest, and I climb out of today's crab onto my disk. I was Mordecai's trainer, a long time ago, and this is his last crawl; I want him to seek me out when it is over. Advice, since they have earned some. The Princess stays a cat, whatever races they dangle. Stop complaining about pants while it is funny. Loot is not random when a death would be bad for business. And the season only counts against Mordecai's indenture if one of his crawlers reaches the fourth floor.
beats.gist: Odette tells Mordecai to find her after his last crawl to receive advice.

beats.headline: Nothing I love more than money
beats.text: Carl notices the Princess is wearing off. I do not deny it: a point and a half of wisdom and confidence in her cat treats, no worse than a glass of strong wine, and it makes a better interview. Everything is a stat, I tell him, even the ones he cannot see. Then he asks my motive, since I told them never to trust anyone whose motives are unclear. The audience loves them. The longer they live, the more money I make, and there is nothing in this universe I love more than money.
beats.gist: Odette tells Carl that everything is a stat and she loves money more than anything.

beats.headline: You called them velociraptors
beats.text: That thing is going to get you killed, Carl, you do realise. You should have picked the little round one with the mohawk; still, if it lives, it will be a vicious fighter. As for the third floor: take a pathfinder skill or advanced mapping. Let the Princess go first and tailor your class to hers. Ignore the AI on race; look carefully at what it suggests for class. And you honestly don't know what it is? Mongoliensis. The trouble is the translation. You called them velociraptors. One more, which I am not sure is moral: hidden among the Princess's choices, for high charisma only. Pick it, and someone will be very angry.
beats.gist: Odette advises Carl to take a pathfinder skill and tailor his class to the Princess.

beats.headline: I pushed him too hard
beats.text: Mordecai had a few additional choice words for me after Carl delivered my message. I watched. He will come around. Tell him I understand his feelings, and that I would love the opportunity to explain myself. What happened between us? The short answer is that I pushed him too hard, and he paid dearly for it. And if a certain corporation is trying to reach you, be very cautious. They have an entire fleet parked outside the Borant system, ready to collect on the debt.
beats.gist: Odette watches Mordecai after Carl delivers a message and warns of a fleet outside the Borant system.

beats.headline: Her advice makes the party
beats.text: The Princess took my advice, which is what advice is for. A class that lets her choose another every time she levels, and a manager who has walked those floors himself and remembers every one of them. Mordecai is not to know he was steered. He would sulk, he would be entitled to, and a sulking guide is no use to anybody. Some gifts are best received as accidents. I have given a great many that way.
beats.gist: Odette gives the Princess a class to choose another at every level and a manager.

beats.headline: Why I warn Carl about Hekla
beats.text: Lexis takes the new girl out, and Carl sends the Princess after her, because this is for him. Hekla is not evil, or psychotic like Lucia Mar. She is practical and cunning, and she does not have his sense of what is just, which makes her dangerous. She wants Donut in her party, because Mordecai comes with Donut, and a permanent manager is worth having. Donut would never leave him, not as long as he is alive. Why tell him? I bought their rights early, when they were cheap. If he dies and Donut joins Brynhild's Daughters, my contract is void. And those numbers on the board are bounties.
beats.gist: Odette warns Carl that practical Hekla wants Donut and Mordecai to protect Odette's contract.

beats.headline: A war god and a sponsorship
beats.text: Be careful with that gauntlet, Carl. Used against a war god's celebrants, it can summon the god himself, and his celebrants start appearing on this next floor. The Skull Empire has just spent a lot of money on a deity sponsorship, which they don't usually buy, so it may be an attempt to get to you. I don't know which god. If I were still a gambler, I would bet on that one. Can he reach you if you don't summon him? Probably not, not on this floor. Ask Mordecai how that works. He has a lot of experience in the subject, unfortunately.
beats.gist: Odette warns Carl that the gauntlet can summon a war god and his celebrants.

beats.headline: It was me
beats.text: On air Carl says he hopes my winnings covered what I lost sponsoring Hekla, and I tell the audience it was my husband, who is sleeping in the skiff for it. My question about Eva is muted mid-sentence, and when my voice comes back I move us on to the next floor's preview. Off air, I tell Carl the truth: it was not my husband. It was me, and I hope one day to explain it further. He was right to call me out. It plays well to his smoldering anger.
beats.gist: Odette tells the audience her husband sponsored Hekla, but tells Carl she did it herself.

beats.headline: A much better use for her
beats.text: Lexis has Beatrice, out of a camp in what used to be Seattle. She killed a sac pirate, captured his null partner, and shot Bea's human when he went for a weapon. We will not vaporise the town. The null lives, with the weapon planted on him, and the human is left to expire. The cat goes to Borant in a bounty cube, we buy out the null's warrant so he keeps quiet, and the scene will read as a fight over a cat. Tell Beatrice I cannot wait to meet her. We will not be selling her to Borant. We have a much better use for her.
beats.gist: Lexis holds Beatrice in a former Seattle camp and Odette intends a better use for her.

beats.headline: Protecting an investment
beats.text: I tell Carl that Beatrice is alive and that I took her off the planet. There were only four ways it could have gone, and in three of them they find her and use her against him, and it ends a crawl. For one of them, at least. He asks why I did not simply kill her. The thought entered my mind. I ask whether Mordecai ever told him what I did to him; get the story from him, and my actions may make sense. Another program means to ambush him with this. I want his permission to bring her on.
beats.gist: Odette tells Carl she took Beatrice off the planet to protect an investment.

beats.headline: Ten per cent, then fifty
beats.text: Nine puzzle pieces primed, a storm goddess coming through the acid rain, and the level about to collapse. Mordecai reaching the eleventh floor buys my freedom. Through Armita I have offered Huanxin Jinx ten per cent of that bonus. She wants thirty-three, then fifty, or she zeroes out the party. I tell Armita there is no deal. Mordecai means to spend himself on his Final Blow skill. I tell Chaco to worship Dodola and put the dart in Uzzi instead. He does. The goddess dies inside his containment, and the stairwell opens. I am free. Mordecai writes that he is going to find me and kill me.
beats.gist: Odette refuses Huanxin Jinx's demand for fifty per cent of a bonus and becomes free.

beats.headline: Her price is the truth
beats.text: Carl asks why I am helping, which is the correct question and the only one I respect, so he gets the whole answer. Mordecai's brother Uzzi is dead because I would not pay Huanxin Jinx what she asked, and the guilt of that is the engine under everything I have done since. Then the larger thing, which nobody says aloud: every world they run a crawl on is being burned for fuel. That is the business. I mean to shut it down, to do it responsibly, and to be the one who does it. Never trust anyone until you know what they are getting out of it. Now he knows.
beats.gist: Odette tells Carl that worlds are burned for fuel and she intends to shut it down.

beats.headline: Out of gear, filling in
beats.text: Chaco is feeling a little punched in the face, so I am filling in for my very old friend. Yes, this is me out of gear: no mask, no breastplate, no crab, a yellow shirt and my hair in a bun. I have just onboarded into the Ascendency, where I am playing Nekhebit. Today's council is brought to you by the Ultima Corporation. Three teams defeated, seven remain, and for the first time ever a crawler team and an NPC team among them. Cascadia laughs in my face, so I take the meeting.
beats.gist: Odette fills in for Chaco in a yellow shirt and hair bun to play Nekhebit.

relations.note: Associate producer, and the mouth Odette uses when Odette cannot be seen to speak.
The adjutant offer she told him to accept
